newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland needs to balance budget to avert crisis - NBP.
newsitem.headline: Poland needs to balance budget to avert crisis - NBP.

text.p: Poland faces a gaping current account deficit and a Czech-style financial crisis in 1998 if it fails to balance next year's budget, a deputy National Bank of Poland president told Rzeczpospolita newspaper.
"If Poland fails to get rid of its budget deficit we are heading for a Czech-style crisis," Rzeczpospolita quoted Witold Kozinski in its Tuesday edition.

Kozinski said the central bank's forecasts showed that if Poland maintained a budget deficit next year the current account trade gap would widen to $16 billion from last year's $8.15 billion and $12 billion projected for this year.
"I don't want to use the word catastrophe, but the situation will really become dramatic," Kozinski said.

He said the $16 billion forecast assumed that Poland would maintain 5.5 percent growth, slash inflation to 9.5 percent and lower the central budget deficit to 1.7 percent of gross domestic product from 2.8 percent planned for this year.

Kozinski said that at $16 billion the trade gap would reach eight percent of GDP, the same level as in the Czech republic which recently had to take drastic measures to prevent further external balance deterioration.
Kozinski said balancing the budget was central for Poland because a large portion of it was spent on consumption.

"The Polish budget is very consumption-oriented and a deficit results in a significant increase in domestic demand, which in turn cannot be absorbed by internal output and creates demand for imports," Kozinski said.

Kozinski said monetary measures such as currency devaluation or an increase in interest rates would have too many negative side-effects and that a fiscal tightening was the only viable way of stabilising 1998 trade gap at this year's levels.
Finance Minister Marek Belka has said the government would aim at a 1998 deficit of two percent or less but the government has yet to approve next year's outline.

Belka, speaking on Monday in New York at a road-show of Poland's $300-million yankee bond, asked investors for patience and said Poland's monetary and fiscal tightening should eventually bear fruit and cool domestic demand and contain the current account gap.
